_doc: Written by tools/mockups/export_ships.mjs from the approved ship mockups (mockup 6, docs/mockups/concord-hull-concepts.html, Concord page v24, sha256 594bb2708517; mockup 7, docs/mockups/krai-ship-concepts.html, Krai page v21, sha256 c911be74453a; mockup 12, docs/mockups/ssarith-ship-concepts.html, Ssarith Hunt page v29, sha256 1cc96bf7794a; mockup 23, docs/mockups/kelvane-ship-concepts.html, Kelvane Institute page v11, sha256 2d4a622346f2; mockup 24, docs/mockups/freighter-concepts.html, the freighters page v15, sha256 27b89877da7b): each ship built intact by its page's own builder and copied out, so this is exactly the approved geometry. Do not edit; re-run the exporter, the only step needed when a mockup changes. ships[].source and factions[].source give the page file's sha256 and published version each ship came from: an export is stale when the page's sha256 differs. Colours are linear RGB, as glTF. Positions are metres in each glb's frame unless a key says mockup space. materials: every exported material by faction/name, with what the page's shader did where the glb carries a PBR stand-in. ships[].shader_params: the per-ship values the hull shader read.

conventions.origin: the centre of the ship's bounding box (all three axes)
conventions.mockup_space: the pages build in +X port, +Y up, +Z bow; p_mockup = (-(x + o.x), y + o.y, -(z + o.z)) for a glb point (x, y, z), o = the ship's origin_offset_m; the hull shaders' tri-planar detail and livery are in mockup space
conventions.nodes: root: the ship id; under it one node per piece of the mockup at the piece's pivot (hull, secondary, neck, command, wing, pod_<side>, pylon_<side>, nacelle_<side>, blade, crest); under each piece its meshes, merged by zone and material, named <piece>[_<zone>]_<material>, and its empties
conventions.empties: mount_turret_<i>, mount_torpedo_<i>, mount_gun_<i>, engine_<i>, deflector, reactor, bridge, bay_<i>, window_<i>, pad_<i> (a carrier's landing pads), light_nav_port / starboard / aft, light_strobe_<side>, light_beacon_dorsal / ventral, light_flood_<i>; facts in glTF extras (colour linear RGB with its hex, kind, radius_m, range_m, direction in the glb frame). A mount's +Y is the way it faces out of the hull; a flood's -Z is the way it shines (as a Godot SpotLight3D).
conventions.not_exported: live lights, additive glows (thruster plumes, the Krai nacelle panels' halos), particles, wires, damage, shields and broken pieces; the windows of the Concord line (drawn by the hull shader, see hull_shader)

detail.channels: albedo: grime and wear in red (green and blue match); normal: tangent-space xy in red and green, 0.5 flat

hull_shader.source: docs/mockups/concord-hull-concepts.html: hullMat(), PAINT_GLSL paint(), winAt(), winRoom(), pools(); docs/mockups/lib/ship-skin.js GLSL.detail()
did: paint(p, n) by uMode: 0 hull, 1 plain armour, 2 nacelle shell, 3 copper rims, 4 livery accent (uStripe), 5 hazard trim, 6 near black.
Hull and plain armour: armour white on top and sides, subhull grey underneath (n.y < -0.72), each 4 m by 2.6 m plate shaded +-3.5%.

Hull (mode 0) also: a subhull grey service band on the sides between y = uBand.x and uBand.y with a dark line at 48% and dark seams every 8 m; grey dorsal seams 0.2 m either side of |x| = uChan; a livery stripe 2.2 m wide at each z in uStripes (uStripeN of them) in uStripe, with a 0.22 m uSeam edge each side, off the service band.
Nacelle shell (mode 2): armour with a subhull grey band 0.7 m wide every 8 m along z.

Detail: the paint times mix(1, grime, 0.9), grime = detail_albedo.png red channel; the normal bent by detail_normal.png xy (whiteout blend), both projected tri-planar in mockup ship space (weights |n|^6), tile_m along z and x by round y and x.
Roughness 0.48 + 0.3 (1 - grime); metalness the material's.

Windows (uWinOn, hull only): 2.2 m cells along z from uWinZ.x to uWinZ.y, one at each deck floor in uDecks (uDeckN of them) + 1.5 m, skipping each fifth cell and the livery stripes, inside the chamfers; a copper rim, black glass (roughness 0.06), and a room behind it drawn by interior mapping, lit with its life-support section.

Floodlight pools (baked hull lights): emissive = paint * pools(p, n), from the light_flood_* empties (position, direction, range, strength); in the page a ship in view swaps its pools for real spot lights (lamp_make).

lamp_make.note: how the page turns each flood pool into a SpotLight for the ship in view: distance = range * distance_per_range, intensity = strength * intensity_per_strength; the first shadow_casters cast shadows

detail.channels: albedo: grime and wear in red (green and blue match); normal: tangent-space xy in red and green, 0.5 flat

did: Base colour: the vertex colours (field steel on the hull, plate on nacelles and blades, bronze bevels) times mix(1, grime, 0.8), grime = detail_albedo.png red channel.
Seams (the darkest grime, seam = 1 - smoothstep(0.45, 0.6, grime)) tinted toward bronze * 0.45 by seam * 0.5.

The normal bent by detail_normal.png xy (whiteout blend), both projected tri-planar in mockup ship space (weights |n|^6), tile_m; the fine detail fades out below about 3 px a seam (metres per pixel 0.012 to 0.05).
Roughness 0.3 + 0.3 (1 - grime) + 0.15 seam, 0.55 under paint; metalness the material's, times (1 - 0.6 paint).

Livery, painted on the side faces (|n.x| > 0.3) where |x| < uLiv2.x + 0.3 m (the hull, not the nacelles): with t = (z - uLiv.x) / (uLiv.y - uLiv.x) and hgt = uLiv.w - uLiv.z, a crimson war stripe centred at y = uLiv.z + hgt (0.28 + 0.3 sw^2), sw = smoothstep(0.62, 0.93, t), half width hgt (0.03 + 0.07 smoothstep(0.1, 0.6, t)) (1 - smoothstep(0.8, 0.94, t)), for t in 0.12 to 0.94; bronze pin lines 0.32 uLiv2.z beyond each edge of it, t in 0.14 to 0.86, 0.05 to 0.1 uLiv2.z wide; bronze battle tallies above it from t = 0.14, pitch 0.75 uLiv2.z, in fives with a gap (uLiv2.y of them), each 0.42 of the pitch wide and 1.5 uLiv2.z tall, 0.9 uLiv2.z above the stripe. Paint = colour * (0.55 + 0.45 grime) * mix(1, 0.85, seam).

livery_uniforms.uLiv: vec4(zMin, zMax, botMin, topMax): the fitted hull's stern and bow z, and its lowest and highest y (mockup ship space, metres)
livery_uniforms.uLiv2: vec4(hbMax, tally, max(1, 0.8 s), 0): the hull's widest half beam (m), the class's battle tallies (CLASSES[id].tally), and the paint scale, s = hull length / 87 m (the frigate's)

hull_shader.source: docs/mockups/lib/baked-fleet.js (on docs/mockups/ssarith-ship-concepts.html): hullLooks(), hullShader() (HULL_GLSL); maps by tools/blender/painted_bake.py --ship
did: Each ship has its own unwrap and its own maps (assets/ships/ssarith/<id>_*.png, named in the ship's shader_params.maps), no tile: base colour (sRGB), ORM (occlusion, roughness, metalness in red, green, blue), a tangent-space normal map (OpenGL, +Y up), emission (sRGB: lamps, light strips), and a light map of the hull lights falling on the plating (linear).

PBR look: albedo = base; roughness and metalness from ORM green and blue (roughness 1, metalness 1 scaled by them); AO from ORM red; emission = the emission map + albedo * pow(light, light_gamma) * k, k the light's strength (0.3 in the page's studio light, 4.5 at night).
The glb's UVs are the bake's, v flipped for glTF (v = 0 the image's top row), so the PNGs map as they stand.
Battle damage as the other factions' hulls (DAMAGE_GLSL, dmgBreak): the hull shader takes the scorch, holes and fracture cells; a broken piece's emission and light map die with it (uLight).
